sources.excerpt: Buzzing Bugs Audio Devices introduce the Bolster Skip to main content Log in Register Subscribe Shop Help 0 items Search SOUND ON SOUND Home SOS For Artists Advertise Information Readers' Ads Competitions Videos Podcasts Case Studies eBooks News Latest All News Search Podcasts Case Studies Readers Ads Forum Latest Posts Search SOS For Artists Readers Ads FAQ Glossary Rules Magazine Latest issue All issues Publication Dates Subscribe Advertise Write for SOS Search Reviews Articles Search Podcasts Glossary Case Studies Techniques Articles Series Search Podcasts Glossary Case Studies People Articles Search Podcasts Glossary Case Studies Sound Advice Articles Search Podcasts Glossary Case Studies Music Business Articles Search Podcasts Glossary Case Studies Set us as a Google preferred source preferred facebook twitter email print You are here Home News Buzzing Bugs Audio Devices introduce the Bolster Published 15/5/26 Fuzz pedal joins UK company's line-up UK-based pedal makers Buzzing Bugs Audio Devices have recently unveiled their latest creation, the Bolster . Said to pay homage to the myths and legends of the company’s home county of Cornwall, the new effect has been named after a folklore giant that lived near the cliffs of Chapel Porth and terrorised the people of the nearby village — an appropriate title for a fuzz pedal! The new arrival is a two-channel design that has been designed to cover a wide range of classic and modern tones. Its main channel employs a silicon transistor circuit, and includes a Volts control that makes it possible to over- or under-supply the circuitry, allowing it to cover everything from Tone Bender-style sounds to “synthy buzzsaws”. Plenty of tone-shaping control is available, with a Shift dial interacting with the input circuitry and a Tone control providing classic Big Muff-style EQ. The More channel then delivers what Buzzing Bugs describe as “a speaker-destroying op-amp one-knob fuzz which offers a monolithic amount of sustain.” Everything comes housed in a rugged die-cast metal enclosure fitted with top-mounted jack sockets. The unit offers true bypass switching, and accepts power from a standard centre-negative 9V DC supply. Bolster, the Cornish Giant, lived near the cliffs of Chapel Porth and terrorised the people of the nearby village. Feasting on children and livestock, Bolster overcame anyone who dared challenge him. Our take on Bolster is a two channel gain monster. The main channel is a silicon transistor high-gain fuzz which ranges from a classic Tone Bender-esque drive, to a synthy buzzsaw by use of starving or saturating the circuit with the VOLTS control. The SHIFT control gives more control over the tone circuit, providing an incredibly flexible EQ range. The MORE channel is a speaker destroying op-amp one-knob fuzz which gives a monolithic amount of sustain. VOLTS - Starve or over-supply the transistors in the circuit to sweep from classic tonebender sounds, through to synth-like gated buzzsaw. Learn more Featured Deal Line 6 Helix Floor used onstage with Ed Sheeran – just £660 at Reverb! Claim Reviews Buzzing Bugs Bolster review – is this the ultimate dual fuzz pedal? Inspired by the bloodthirsty folklore of Cornwall, BB’s latest stompbox covers just about every fuzzy tone imaginable… and it’s an absolute beast Buzzing Bugs Bolster. Image: Richard Purvis by Richard Purvis August 10, 2026 by Richard Purvis August 10, 2026 When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Review Overview Our rating 10 Our verdict ⊕ Two monster fuzz circuits that sound even more monstrous together ⊕ Voltage control offers classic gating effects to the left… ⊕ …and buzzy quasi-synth sounds to the right ⊕ Tone controls are subtle but clever ⊖ Limited availability outside the UK Surely the best Buzzing Bugs pedal yet, this is a fabulous dual fuzz that packs a surprisingly wide range of high-gain tones into a simple and approachable format. £179, buzzingbugsfx.com If you name a fuzz pedal after an evil scary giant, it’d better be pretty frickin’ fearsome. To that end, the Buzzing Bugs Bolster has been designed with a scorching high-gain circuit on one side… and an even more scorching one on the other. READ MORE: Teaching Machines FuzzBillion review: is this the most ambitious and unique dirt pedal ever made? The giant in question is a figure of Cornish legend – and that’s no coincidence, because the UK’s southernmost county is where this smart-looking pedal is made. But while the original Bolster apparently terrorised villages, ate children and was very inconsiderate to his wife, this one only wants to spook your eardrums. Image: Richard Purvis What is it? I spent a good half-hour noodling away with the Bolster before I realised something quite important: the ‘more’ side isn’t just an extra dose of gain to add to the main business on the right, but a whole separate fuzz circuit in itself. So this is a classic double stomper, offering instant access to two individual sounds plus an apocalyptic ‘both’ option. The right-hand fuzz is a silicon transistor type, with controls for gain, tone, output level, volts (for bias-tampering effects ) and shift (for thinning out the bass at the input stage). The left channel skips all of that and keeps things simple with a single level knob for its extra-feisty op- amp fuzz. This could get brutal. Image: Richard Purvis Sounds “Could get brutal”? It starts brutal! The right-hand channel is up first, and it’s a blast. Keep the volts knob set at noon for normal biasing, and what comes out is the very nicest kind of thick, smooth, aggressive fuzz, with a good balance between body and clarity. If you want to change that balance, you have two options. Turning down the shift knob brings a leaner, more focused sound – a great match for humbuckers that are at risk of succumbing to flub – while the standard tone control turns out to be… well, not exactly standard. Crank it up and, rather than opening up the very highest frequencies, it gives a boost in the bitey upper-mids zone. Neither of these knobs will dramatically transform the tone of the Bolster, but between the two of them you’ve got an awful lot of tweaking power. The one-knob fuzz isn’t entirely different in character but feels more open, with a distinctly mids-scooped voicing. On its own it sounds properly gigantic… and when you use both sides together, it somehow gets even bigger in a way that can make it difficult to persuade yourself to stop playing.
